v49_frozen_retrieval_benchmark.purpose: FAST MVP lane directive: the smallest executable retrieval/counter-authority benchmark that can falsify the product. The frozen reality benchmark measures recorded ANSWER artifacts; this one measures whether the frozen controlling authorities are reachable at all in independent OpenCaseLaw retrieval, in which query language, at what rank, with what duplicates and at what latency. Baseline = one plain /decisions search per (question, language, channel) with no query-map/counter-authority machinery, per the lane directive.

Authority sets re-owned from the frozen reality benchmark (sha ff57f556...); known-counter ids = union of counter-classified cited_decisions rows across accepted reality_check legs (label soundness NOT re-verified; stated in the spec).

critical_findings.citation_heritage_dense_superiority: CORRECTED (v35 citation-heritage fairness audit, run 38039706350): dense multilingual-e5 embeddings CARRY citation-relatedness signal (self-pair-free AUC 0.719 cp64 on the ORIG relation; 0.69 DIRECT; 0.92-0.97 on shared-citation relations), but are NOT superior to a TF-IDF citation representation on identical matched pairs (dense_cp64 0.7189 vs cited_decisions_tfidf 0.7159, margin +0.003, 95% CI [-0.034,+0.037]). The earlier 'dense 0.79-0.85 > TF-IDF citation 0.71-0.74' comparison was an artifact of (a) mismatch of pair sets (dense on 730 pairs, TF-IDF on 1020) and (b) 17% self-pairs (d,d) inflating both by ~0.045 AUC. A full-dimensional citation representation (binary outgoing-citation Jaccard) beats dense on DIRECT citations (0.7735 vs 0.6924) and is an oracle on shared-citation relations (1.000). Product implication: build the citation-heritage view from the citation graph for corpora with resolved citations; use dense embeddings only as a text-only proxy when citation metadata is absent. Dense remains COMPLEMENTARY (cross-lingual view, linear hybrid) and FAILS the jurist gate at all scales. Does not affect the two-mode tradeoff.
critical_findings.section_crosslingual_hierarchy: Section-specific cross-lingual evaluation COMPLETE for all three sections at 1K sample scale. Sachverhalt (facts, n=359) SUPERIOR: cp_64 cross_lang_same_branch=0.282, invariance_gap=0.187. Dispositiv (holding, n=538) INTERMEDIATE: cp_64 cross_lang_same_branch=0.150, invariance_gap=0.397. Erwaegungen (reasoning, n=510) POOREST: cp_64 cross_lang_same_branch=0.094, invariance_gap=0.452. Center projection improves all (sachverhalt gap 0.304->0.187, erwaegungen 0.538->0.452, dispositiv 0.575->0.397). Legal facts align best cross-lingually; holdings retain some alignment; reasoning is most language-specific. Full corpus density BLOCKED pending section extraction at 174k scale.
critical_findings.linear_hybrids_scale_dependency: Weight sweep at 22-year (144k) reveals OPTIMAL w=0.4 for cited_decisions_tfidf (JP=0.6725, LangDom=0.6539 BOTH PASS) and w=0.3 for outcome_hybrid_0.5 (JP=0.6115, LangDom=0.7477 BOTH PASS). At 19-year optimal was w=0.3 for both. At 15-year linear_hybrid05_concat FAILS (JP=0.473). Scale shifts optimal weight toward denser semantic contribution at larger scale. But BOTH still BELOW TF-IDF baseline (JP=0.784/0.789). Optimal weight shifts toward TF-IDF dominance (w=0.3-0.4 dense / 0.6-0.7 TF-IDF). Citation signals dominate jurist preference; semantic signals add cross-lingual benefit but dilute legal relevance.
critical_findings.two_mode_tradeoff_fundamental: Citation/Outcome (TF-IDF hybrids): LangDom~0.48, JP~0.78, CiteIndep~14%. Semantic Embeddings (center_projected): LangDom~0.83-0.98, JP~0.05-0.43, CiteIndep~37%. Linear Hybrids: LangDom~0.58-0.80, JP~0.61-0.67 (optimal weight), intermediate. NO single representation dominates all three metrics at any scale. TF-IDF citation hybrids = PRIMARY product mode (jurist preference, branch clustering). Dense embeddings = COMPLEMENTARY modes (citation heritage view, cross-lingual view, linear hybrid complement).
critical_findings.dense_embeddings_fail_jurist_gate_all_sc: At 3yr ACCEPTED (19k): JP=0.39-0.42 FAIL. At 15yr (92k): JP=0.288 FAIL. At 19yr (122k): JP=0.37 FAIL. At 20yr (130k): JP=0.05 CATASTROPHIC FAIL. At 22yr (144k): JP=0.43 FAIL. Dense semantic embeddings DO NOT PASS jurist gate at any scale tested; performance degrades catastrophically at 20yr then partially recovers at 22yr. critical_findings.true_oos_juristpref_ceiling: True OOS JuristPref ceiling ~0.53 < 0.7 factory target. No representation (TF-IDF, dense, hybrid) achieves the factory jurist preference target under true out-of-sample conditions. TF-IDF baseline JP=0.78 is evaluated on same data used for SVD fitting (known leakage, though v8 holdout showed minimal impact: JP -0.015 to -0.020).
critical_findings.legal_tfidf_bge_corpus_negative: Legal TF-IDF from bge_ corpus (published BGE volumes, 6,243 decisions, 2000-2021) FAILS adversarial suite (6-8/14 PASS vs 14/14 baseline). ALL variants FAIL citation heritage (AUC ~0.5), branch kNN (0.26-0.39), multilingual invariance, cross-language pairs. They PASS language dominance (LangDom~0.49-0.50) -- confirming legal signals are cross-lingual. Root cause: corpus mismatch -- bge_ IDs don't map to bger_ evaluation corpus; signal coverage deficits: cited decisions 0.06%, outcomes 0%, Erwaegungen 64%. citation_heritage_claim_correction.rule: dense must beat best TF-IDF citation rep by >= +0.02 AUC on identical matched self-pair-free pairs
citation_heritage_claim_correction.conclusion: Dense citation-heritage AUC is statistically indistinguishable from the TF-IDF citation representation on identical matched pairs. The accepted 'dense 0.79-0.85 > TF-IDF 0.71-0.74' claim is a pair-set mismatch + self-pair artifact. For citation-heritage views, use the citation graph / a full-dimensional citation representation; dense is justified only as a text-only proxy when citations are unavailable. Resolves cross-lane contradiction in favour of the evaluation lane's retraction.

Identical matched self-pair-free ORIG (606/834): dense_cp64 0.7189 vs best text-only regeste_full_text_hybrid_0.7 0.5866 (margin +0.1324, CI +0.0925..+0.1709); DIRECT hard-matched (5255/6008): 0.6924 vs 0.5616 (+0.1308). full_text_tfidf_light (used in the original non-comparable claim) is NOT the strongest text-only rep (0.5308; regeste_tfidf is the weakest at 0.4850, below chance).
